m-greenacres|2026-11-16|13d0eed6|4048c00.title: Analysis Staff is requesting authorization to piggyback Palm Beach County Contract/Project No. 2024050, effective July 2, 2024, through July 1, 2027, awarded to Ranger Construction Industries, Inc. The contract provides established pricing for asphalt milling and resurfacing services, allowing the City to complete the roadway improvements in a cost- effective and efficient manner. Ranger Construction Industries, Inc. provided a quotation in the amount of $234,204.56 for the asphalt refurbishment of Biscayne Drive and Biscayne Boulevard. The proposed work includes milling and resurfacing the existing asphalt pavement, manhole adjustments, and making additional roadway repairs in approximately seven areas affected by tree root intrusions. These locations will require deeper excavation to address the underlying root issues before repairing and resurfacing the roadway. The quotation is based on the pricing established under Palm Beach County’s annual asphalt milling and resurfacing contract.

Chair Miller said there was another amendment and invited Jerry Holland, Supervisor of Elections, to explain the amendment. First, he said there were two methods for post-election audits. The current method is a hand-counted audit of a randomly selected race and precincts chosen by the Canvassing Board and county judge. He said the second method utilizes technology called Clear Ballot, which takes a picture of each oval on every ballot and audits 100 percent of ballots. He said the equipment was separate from the machines used to tabulate votes. He said 32 of Florida’s 67 counties have adopted the technology, using county funding. Mr. Holland said the State wants all counties to use this technology and has provided funding for counties to purchase it by the end of the year. This bill would appropriate state funds to purchase the equipment. He said the amendment would identify the company as Clear Ballot, which is the only company certified to do post-election audits in the state. 

The amendment was moved and seconded. 

Ms. Staffopoulos clarified that the amendment would add language to the bill for a direct contract with Clear Ballot that would be authorized under Section 126.108(g) of the Ordinance Code, which would provide an exemption from competitive solicitation.

Through extensive public input and Unmet Needs and Mitigation Needs Assessments in the Action Plan, the City determined the need to create the Non-Profit Community Support Services (NPCSS) program to address the increased need for essential community services as a result of the qualifying disasters. m-tallahassee|2026-11-18|1d632697|c7f4ce.title: Section 420.9075 Florida Statute and Chapter 67 -37, Florida Administrative Code, states: “A county or an eligible municipality may not exceed the 5 percent limitation on administrative costs, unless its governing body finds, by resolution, that 5 percent of the local housing distribution plus 5 percent of program income is insufficient to adequately pay the necessary costs of administering the local housing assistance plan.” Section 420.9075 Florida Statute and Chapter 67-37, Florida Administrative Code, further states: “The cost of administering the program may not exceed 10 percent of the local housing distribution plus 5 percent of program income deposited into the trust fund, except that small counties, as defined in s. 120.52(19), and eligible municipalities receiving a local housing distribution of up to $350,000 may use up to 10 percent of program income for administrative costs. ” The applicable local jurisdiction has adopted the above findings in the resolution attached as Exhibit E.

Improvements may be exterior, interior or a combination of interior/exterior. Grants are contingent upon the availability of funds in the Tallahassee CRA budget. Grant awards are also contingent upon a demonstrated benefit to the CRA district and compliance with the Downtown or Greater Frenchtown/Southside Redevelopment Plan. Additional eligibility requirements and program features are described below.
